# Text Analysis Project {#sec-text-project}

## Project Overview {#sec-text-project-overview}

The goal of this project is to build a reproducible workflow for collecting, storing, and analyzing text from online articles.

We will use:

- *Excel*: as the original source of the article list.
- *R*: to import, clean, scrape, and analyze the data.
- *SQLite*: to store and organize the data.
- *Quarto*: to document and present the final analysis.

The general workflow is:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Excel] --> B[R]
    B --> C[SQLite Database]
    C --> D[R: Extract Text]
    D --> E[Update SQLite Database]
    E --> F[R: Prepare Text]
```

The goal is to create a workflow that can be reused for future text-analysis projects.

Before getting started, please review @sec-databases-sql-r for an introduction to databases, SQL, SQLite, and working with SQL in R.

## Extract the Article Text {#sec-text-project-extract-text}

### Goal {#sec-text-project-extract-text-goal}

Use the URLs stored in the database to retrieve the text from each article.

This work will be completed in R.

The final data should contain the original article information plus a new variable:

```         
article_text
```

### Tasks {#sec-text-project-extract-text-tasks}

- [ ] Retrieve the article URLs from SQLite.
- [ ] Test text extraction using one article.
- [ ] Inspect the extracted text.
- [ ] Create a reusable function for extracting article text.
- [ ] Apply the function to all articles.
- [ ] Identify articles that could not be extracted.
- [ ] Create the `article_text` column.

### Example Code {#sec-text-project-extract-text-example-code}

Below is sample code to help with text extraction:

```         
library(rvest)

url <- "https://example.com/news/article"

page <- read_html(url)

article_text <- page |>
  html_elements("p") |>
  html_text2() |>
  paste(collapse = " ")

article_text
```

::: callout-tip

#### Writing Functions {#sec-text-project-extract-text-writing-functions}

Instead of repeating this code for each article, create a function that takes a URL and returns the article text. This will allow the same process to be applied across all article URLs.\
:::

## Final Workflow {#sec-text-project-final-workflow}

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Excel Article List] --> B[Import into R]
    B --> C[Create SQLite Database]
    C --> D[Retrieve URLs into R]
    D --> E[Extract Article Text]
    E --> F[Update SQLite Database]
    F --> G[Retrieve Data into R]
```

The goal is not only to complete this analysis, but to understand the workflow well enough to repeat it with a new collection of documents in the future.

## Key Takeaways {#sec-text-project-key-takeaways}

- Excel can be used as the original source of article information, while SQLite can become the main working database.
- R can connect directly to SQLite using the `DBI` and `RSQLite` packages.
- SQLite makes it easier to store, organize, retrieve, and update article data as the project grows.
- SQL commands can be sent to the database from R using functions such as `dbGetQuery()`.
- A unique `article_id` helps keep each article connected to its text and future analysis results.
- Article text can be extracted in R and then written back to the SQLite database.
- SQL is useful for filtering, counting, grouping, and retrieving data before analysis.
- R remains the primary tool for text cleaning, tokenization, sentiment analysis, visualization, and other text-mining tasks.

## Key Functions and Commands {#sec-text-project-key-functions}

### Excel and Data Import {#sec-text-project-key-functions-excel-and-data-import}

| Function       | Purpose                            |
|----------------|------------------------------------|
| `read_excel()` | Import an Excel file into R        |
| `head()`       | View the first rows of a dataset   |
| `str()`        | Inspect the structure of a dataset |
| `nrow()`       | Count the number of rows           |
| `duplicated()` | Check for duplicate values         |
| `is.na()`      | Check for missing values           |

### Connecting R to SQLite {#sec-text-project-key-functions-connecting-r-to-sqlite}

|                  |                                        |
|------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Function         | Purpose                                |
| `dbConnect()`    | Connect R to a database                |
| `SQLite()`       | Tell R to use SQLite                   |
| `dbDisconnect()` | Close the database connection          |
| `dbListTables()` | List the tables stored in the database |

### Reading and Writing Database Data {#sec-text-project-key-functions-reading-and-writing-database-data}

|                  |                                                   |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Function         | Purpose                                           |
| `dbWriteTable()` | Write an R data frame to SQLite                   |
| `dbReadTable()`  | Read an entire SQLite table into R                |
| `dbGetQuery()`   | Send a SQL query to SQLite and return the results |
| `dbExecute()`    | Send a SQL command that changes the database      |

### Basic SQL Commands {#sec-text-project-key-functions-basic-sql-commands}

|            |                                      |
|------------|--------------------------------------|
| Command    | Purpose                              |
| `SELECT`   | Choose columns or values to retrieve |
| `FROM`     | Identify the table being queried     |
| `WHERE`    | Filter records                       |
| `COUNT()`  | Count records                        |
| `GROUP BY` | Group records before summarizing     |
| `ORDER BY` | Sort query results                   |
| `UPDATE`   | Change existing records              |
| `IS NULL`  | Identify missing database values     |

### Web Scraping {#sec-text-project-key-functions-web-scraping}

|                   |                                          |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Function          | Purpose                                  |
| `read_html()`     | Read the HTML from a webpage             |
| `html_elements()` | Select elements from a webpage           |
| `html_text2()`    | Extract text from selected HTML elements |
